findings.text: **[Medium / P1] Verify saved process identity before stopping a retained run's server.** A `--keep-scratch` run retains `pids.jsonl` containing only `{role,pid,at}`. Later manual cleanup reduces those records to numeric PIDs here. If Linux has reused an old `hosted-server` PID (or wrapper PID) for a newer unrelated server on this port, `ownedBy` returns true and the current matching PID/state files pass `agree`, so cleanup invokes `start:hosted --stop`. That command validates the newer server's own start time, not its relationship to the retained run, and stops it. An exact-source diagnostic at this head, with old saved PID123 and newer PID123/start9000/different runId, issued `--stop` with `preserved: []`. This violates `docs/development.md:83` (a verification run stops only a server it started) and requires no check-then-act race. Record the original process start/boot identity and run identity, validate both direct-PID and wrapper-ancestry ownership against those saved values, and preserve records with missing or stale proof. Add a retained-scratch/PID-reuse regression requiring the newer process and its files to survive. The new inner ownership checks do not cover this later outer cleanup.

tests.name: a retained row naming the pid of a newer, unrelated server (same pid, different start, different run) stops nothing and is reported preserved
a retained row of the old shape ({ role, pid, at }, no start) proves nothing: no stop, the server is preserved
a retained row with a start but another run's name proves nothing either
a saved ancestor whose pid now runs a process with another start does not own the server under it
